newsitem.title: FRANCE: 22 people die at end of Ramadan in Algeria - papers. [CORRECTED 10:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: 22 people die at end of Ramadan in Algeria - papers. [CORRECTED 10:00 GMT]

text.p: Twenty-two people, including four (corrects from five) families, have been killed in Algiers and nearby towns in weekend violence coinciding with the end of Ramadan and the feast of Eid al-Fitr, Algerian newspapers said on Monday.

Algeria's Liberte newspaper said suspected Moslem guerrillas on Friday killed 14 people, members of three (corrects from four) families, in the Moslem fundamentalist stronghold of Eucalyptus on the southern edge of Algiers.
A man, his wife and their baby were killed on Saturday in Beaufresier suburb in the north of Algiers, the newspaper said.
Suspected guerrillas shot dead two people on Saturday in Meftah, south of Algiers, said El Watan newspaper.
Two suspected rebels were killed on Saturday, their bodies blown apart by a bomb they were carrying, in Bougara in Blida province, about 50 km (30 miles) south of Aligers.
The same day, gunmen thought to be Moslem guerrrillas killed a mosque preacher in Damous, in Tipaza province, 60 km (40 miles west of Algiers, said El Watan.
